units.title: Interval Bakry–Émery growth gives backward contraction
units.statement: On an ordered interval [s,t], a differentiable scalar interpolation whose derivative dominates r times its value satisfies the exact backward endpoint contraction.
assumptions: Φ has the supplied genuine two-sided derivative Φ' at every point of [s,t].
No sign condition on Φ or r is required; s=t is allowed.

steps.title: Attach the inverse exponential weight
steps.text: Multiply the interpolation by the factor that cancels growth at rate r.

steps.title: Show the weighted derivative is nonnegative
steps.text: The derivative bound makes both factors in W' nonnegative.
steps.lean: Use sub_nonneg and positivity of Real.exp.

steps.title: Compare the endpoints
steps.text: Derivative monotonicity gives W(s)≤W(t); evaluating the exponential weight yields the desired contraction.
steps.lean: Apply monotoneOn_of_deriv_nonneg on Icc s t and simplify both endpoints.

units.lean_statement: The closed and open interval scopes, exact derivative witnesses, endpoint order, and constants are explicit.
units.lean_proof: The proof makes the exponentially weighted interpolation monotone and evaluates it at the two endpoints.
units.boundary: This scalar theorem does not build a Markov semigroup or prove its carré-du-champ derivative, Γ₂ curvature bound, or terminal energy identity.
